items.title: 김정은, G20 앞 訪中 가능성… 美 압박하며 ‘대화 문턱 높이기’
items.snippet: 다음 달 14일 미국에서 열리는 주요 20개국(G20) 정상회의를 앞두고 북한 김정은 국무위원장의 방중 가능성이 거론된다. 중국 선전 아시아태평양경제협력체(APEC) 정상회의에서 미-중-러 정상이 북한 문제를 협의한 가운데 김 위원장이 방중을 통해 시진핑(習近平) 중국 국가주석과 만나 북-미 대화 등에 대해 논의할 수 있다는 것. 김 위원장은 이달 23일에는 “패권도 팽창도 추구하지 않는다”며 마코 루비오 미 국무장관에 호응하는 메시지를 발신한 데 이어 25일엔 “(핵 보유) 합헌적 지위를 부정하면 선전포고”라며 수위 높은 위협을 쏟아냈다. 냉온탕을 오가는 메시지로 북-미 대화 문턱을 높이며 줄다리기에 나선 것이라는 분석이 나온다.● 美서 열리는 G20 앞두고 김정은 방중 가능성최근 정부는 김 위원장의 방중 가능성을 염두에 두고 중국 단둥 지...

items.title: 최민희 징계 확정땐 차기 총선 출마 못해… 친청 “김민석도 징계”
items.snippet: 더불어민주당 윤리심판원이 27일 최민희 최고위원에게 당원 자격정지 2년의 중징계 처분을 내린 것은 친청(친정청래)계를 향한 강력한 경고장을 날린 것으로 풀이된다. 당원 자격정지는 1개월부터 2년까지 기간을 정할 수 있는 만큼 최 최고위원에게 제명을 제외한 최고 수준의 징계를 내렸기 때문이다. 이에 따라 최 최고위원은 수석최고위원직이 박탈되는 것은 물론이고 2028년 총선에서 민주당 후보로 출마할 길이 막히게 됐다. 그동안 최고위원회의 등에서 김민석 대표 등 친명(친이재명)계와 앞장서서 대립각을 세우던 최 최고위원에 대한 중징계를 두고 친청계는 김 대표 사퇴를 요구하는 등 당내 계파 갈등이 전면전 수준으로 고조되고 있다.● 반복된 설화에 가중 처벌 받은 崔 이창환 윤리심판원장은 이날 서울 여의도 중앙당사에서 열린 윤리심판원 회의 뒤 최 최고위원...

items.title: 박홍근 “법사위가 상원이냐”… 민주당 장관이 與의원 이례적 비판
items.snippet: 더불어민주당 4선 의원인 박홍근 기획예산처 장관이 지역 예산 관련 여당 의원의 질의에 답변을 거부하면서 국회 법제사법위원회 전체회의가 개회 15분 만에 정회하는 등 파행했다. 박 장관은 민주당 소속 서영교 법제사법위원장에게 “여기(법사위)가 상원(上院)인가”라고 작심 비판하는 등 예산을 두고 여당 의원들과 거칠게 충돌했다. 법사위 민주당 간사인 김의겸 의원이 27일 서울 여의도 국회에서 열린 법사위 전체회의에서 박 장관에게 “새만금 사업 잘 아시지요”라고 질의를 시작하자 박 장관은 “예산 관련 질문은 여기서는 답변 안 드리겠다”고 잘라 말했다. 이에 김 의원은 “뵙기 어려우니 이런 자리를 빌려서라도 질문하겠다”고 했고, 박 장관은 “법사위는 고유 역할이 있지 않느냐. 예산결산특별위원회에서 이미 충분히 얘기했고 소위원회에서 심사하고 있기 때문에...

items.title: ‘하명 징계’ 싸움에 리더십 실종 국힘… 장동혁 “한동훈 복당해도 다시 징계”
items.snippet: 국민의힘 중앙윤리위원회가 무소속 한동훈 의원과 친한(친한동훈)계 인사들에 대한 징계를 결정하는 과정에서 장동혁 대표가 개입했다는 ‘하명 징계’ 의혹이 확산되는 가운데 “당이 리더십 진공상태로 치닫고 있다”는 지적이 나오고 있다. 당 안팎에서는 한 의원 복당을 주장하고 나선 친한계에 대한 피로감을 호소하는 기류도 감지되고 있다. 한 초선 의원은 27일 본보와의 통화에서 전날 최고위원회의에서 장 대표 측 최고위원과 친한계 최고위원이 정면으로 충돌한 데 대해 “정치적 리더십이 전혀 없는 정당이 됐다”고 평가했다. 당권파 최고위원들과 친한계 우재준 청년최고위원이 공개 충돌하자 정점식 원내대표는 “에이 당 꼬라지하고는”이라며 회의장을 먼저 나섰고, 장 대표는 이어 비공개 회의에서 우 최고위원을 향해 ‘탈당과 창당이라는 좋은 제도가 있다’고 말한 것으로...

items.title: 李 “책임 제대로 물어야 내란 종식”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 27일 청와대에서 열린 사회대개혁위원회 출범 1주년 간담회에서 발언하고 있다. 이 대통령은 이날 간담회에서 “12·3 내란 책임자들에게 헌정 유린에 대한 합당한 책임을 물을 때, 완전한 종식이 이뤄질 것”이라고 했다.

items.title: 이달 급여 1.9억 실수령 강금실… 재산 총액 2억6495만원 신고
items.snippet: 강금실 국가정보원장 후보자가 국회에 예금과 자신의 법무법인 출자지분 등 약 2억6495만 원을 신고한 가운데, 후보자가 올해 11월 한 달에만 이 법무법인에서 급여로 3억4000여만 원이 책정돼 실제로 1억9000만 원을 수령한 것으로 나타났다. 27일 국회에 제출된 강 후보자의 인사청문요청안 등에 따르면 강 후보자는 재산으로 예금 2억3495만9000원과 법무법인 원의 출자지분 2%에 대한 가액 3000만 원 등 2억6495만9000원을 신고했다. 해당 금액은 26일 기준으로 작성됐다. 동시에 그는 이 법무법인에서 11월 급여로 3억4095만6600원을 받았다. 강 후보자 측은 “급여 및 상여금을 포함한 금액으로 소득세 등을 납부하고 예금을 적법하게 신고했다”고 밝혔다. 강 후보자는 본인 명의 부동산 소유권이나 전세권, 채무 등은 보유한 내...

items.snippet: 윤석열 정부 당시 대통령 관저 이전 공사에 필요한 비용을 마련하기 위해 행정안전부 예산을 불법 전용하도록 지시한 혐의로 기소된 김대기 전 대통령비서실장이 1심에서 징역형의 집행유예를 선고받았다. 서울중앙지법 형사합의36부(부장판사 이정엽)는 27일 직권남용권리행사방해 등 혐의로 기소된 김 전 실장에게 징역 2년에 집행유예 3년을 선고했다. 함께 재판에 넘겨졌던 김오진 전 대통령관리비서관과 윤재순 전 대통령총무비서관은 이날 각각 징역 1년에 집행유예 2년을 선고받았다. 구속 상태로 재판을 받아온 김 전 실장과 윤 전 비서관은 판결 선고 뒤 구치소에서 풀려났다. 재판부는 김 전 실장 등이 2022년 관저 이전 공사를 맡았던 업체인 21그램에 추가 공사비를 지급하기 위해 행안부 정부청사관리본부 공무원들에게 본부 예산 20억9000만 원을 전용하도록...

items.title: 우크라이나에서 몽골, 말라위까지… 이 부부의 길엔 국경이 없다
items.snippet: 1994년 우크라이나 서부 도시 테르노필의 한 치과. 열다섯 살쯤 된 남학생이 뒤로 젖혀지지도 않는 의자에 앉아 신경 치료를 받고 있었다. 통증을 줄이기 위해 마취를 해야 했지만, 나라 전체가 겪는 경제난 탓에 병원에는 마취제가 없었다. 그런데도 학생은 의자 손잡이를 꼭 잡은 채 얼굴을 조금 찌푸릴 뿐 소리 한 번 지르지 않고 묵묵히 견뎌냈다. 단기 의료 봉사로 우크라이나를 방문해 이를 지켜보던 당시 34세 치과 의사 강지헌씨는 다짐했다. 의료 인프라가 열악한 이 나라에 다시 와서 환자들의 아픔을 조금이라도 덜어주겠다고.

items.title: 하나의 칼집에 박힌 두 자루의 칼
items.snippet: 지난주 내내 특별전 준비로 전시실 작업이 있었다. 전시실 내 인테리어 공사가 마무리되어 유물을 전시실로 옮겨 와서 배치하는 일이다. 전시품 배치는 미리 구상하고 평면도와 입면도를 보며 여러 번 검토하지만, 실제로 유물을 놓아 보면 이미지로 시뮬레이션해 본 것과는 달라 받침대나 위치를 바꾸기도 하고, 일부 유물은 추가로 받치고 고정하기도 한다. 지난주에는 대학수학능력시험과 관련하여 나날이 강력해지는 AI의 위력을 실감할 수 있었기에, 전시실에서 지난한 작업을 하던 일부 직원들은 약간의 소외감을 느끼기도 한 것 같다. 그러나 디지털이 만들어낸 가상의 세계가 커질수록 물질성을 직접 느끼는 박물관 경험은 더욱 귀하게 쓰일 것이라 믿고 있다.

items.title: 검찰 이빨 다 뽑은 이재명 시대… 절대 ‘피해자’가 되지 맙시다
items.snippet: 작년 10월 20일, 김창민 영화감독은 아들과 함께 경기 구리시의 식당을 찾았다가 다른 테이블에 있던 이들과 소음 문제로 다툰 끝에 뇌사 상태에 빠졌다. 사인은 심한 구타로 인한 두개골 골절과 뇌출혈이었는데, 발달장애가 있던 아들은 그 사건을 목격한 뒤 증상이 악화됐단다. 문제는 그 이후 불거졌다. 20·30대 남성 6명이 김 감독을 위협하는 데 가담했고, 그중에는 폭력 전과가 있는 이도 있었지만, 경찰은 단 1명(이씨)만, 그것도 중상해 혐의를 적용해 불구속 송치했다.

items.title: 3주간 스마트폰 없이 지냈더니 기적이 일어났다?
items.snippet: “수능 최하위권이었다. 전국 도보 일주를 하다 스마트폰을 잃어버려 3주간 디지털 디톡스(digital detox·온라인 과의존 해독)를 하게 됐다. 신기한 일이 일어났다. 갑자기 집중력이 높아지고 어려운 글이 이해됐다. 고려대 정외과, 그리고 서울대 치대에 합격했다. 이어 법학적성시험(LEET)에서 사상 첫 만점자로….”

items.title: 수능시험 날의 생각들
items.snippet: 중국과 조선의 과거제도, 일본의 고등문관시험, 우리나라의 고등고시와 행정고시·사법시험 등은 공정한 시험에 의해 신분 상승의 길을 열어 사회적 갈등을 완화하고 정치적 안정을 유지하는 역할을 했습니다. 비록 한계는 있었지만, 가난하거나 권세 없는 집안의 자녀도 자신의 노력과 능력으로 시험을 통해 높은 지위에 오를 수 있다는 희망을 품었기 때문입니다. 이른바 ‘개천에서 용이 난다’는 말도 이러한 믿음의 표현입니다. 어떤 학자는 이런 제도가 없었으면 반란은 더 빈번히 발생했을 것이고, 공산화도 더 쉽게 진행되었을 것이라고도 합니다. 우연일지도 모르지만 실제로 중국의 경우, 과거제도가 폐지된 뒤에 신해혁명이 일어났고 결국 공산화의 길로 들어섰습니다.

items.title: 주식의 신은 이렇게 말했다
items.snippet: 김남우는 주식 고수로 정평이 나 있었지만, 큰 인기는 없었다. 재미없는 말만 입에 달고 살았으니까. “주식은 건실하게 지수 추종만 하면 돼. 미국이 망하지 않는 한 절대로 손해는 안 본다니까.”

items.title: 남들이 다 사 갈까 봐 급히 또 주문했다
items.snippet: 새벽 의림지에 하얀 안개가 꼈다. 둑과 길 위로 걷고 뛰는 이들이 보였다. 바람은 불지 않고 물결도 일지 않았다. 어릴 적 살던 부산 영도에서 밖을 바라보면 늘 일렁이는 파도였다. 오고 가는 커다란 배와 세찬 바람을 맞으면 어린 마음에도 어디론가 떠나고 싶었다. 중년이 되어 의림지 앞에 서니 가슴이 뛰기보다 잔잔해졌다. 그러나 제천에는 이제 KTX가 다닌다. 여전히 조용한 동네이고 사람들은 의뭉스러운 충청도 사투리를 쓰지만, 의림지에서 제천역으로 향하는 국도 사이로 시끌벅적한 가게들도 여럿 생겼다. 저수지 주변을 한참 걷고 온 탓인지 가볍게 빵 몇 조각만 있어도 충분할 것 같았다. 아침 8시, 문을 연 빵집을 찾다 ‘솔솔’이라는 곳을 찾았다. 발효빵을 비롯해 식사빵을 주로 파는 듯 보였다. 선택지가 없었다. 대로변 아담한 빵집에는 작은 주차장...

items.title: 트레비 분수의 동전이 줄어든 이유
items.snippet: 이탈리아 로마 트레비 분수에 동전 던져본 적 있으십니까. 이 분수에 동전을 던지면 로마에 다시 올 수 있거나 소원이 이루어진다는 속설이 있죠. 1732년부터 30년에 걸쳐 만든 트레비 분수는 로마 여행의 필수 코스로 꼽힙니다.

items.title: “노력은 부질없고 앞날은 막막”… 번지는 ‘AI 블루’
items.snippet: “요즘 인공지능(AI) 때문에 우울해요. 열심히 노력하는 게 무슨 의미가 있나 싶어서요.”

items.title: 기상 알람은 필요하지만 스마트폰은 안 쓰고 싶다
items.snippet: 지난 5월 일본 가전 회사 발뮤다는 신제품으로 탁상시계 ‘더 클락’을 내놓았다. 스마트폰이 시계 기능은 물론 기상 알람, 타이머 역할까지 대신해 주는 시대에 굳이 수십만 원짜리 시계를 선보인 것이다. 이 시계엔 최신 가전제품들이 앞다퉈 탑재하는 사물인터넷(IoT) 연동이나 음성 인공지능(AI) 기능도 들어 있지 않다. 대신 눈뜨자마자 스마트폰을 집어 들고, 잠들 때도 이를 머리맡에 두는 현대인들이 잠시나마 스마트폰과 거리를 두게 하는 데 초점을 맞췄다. 기존 탁상시계의 알람과 타이머 기능은 그대로 갖추되, 시침과 분침 대신 LED로 시간을 표시해 어두운 공간에서도 시간을 확인할 수 있도록 했다. 또 이른바 ‘백색소음’을 들으며 잠을 청하는 사람들을 위해 빗소리와 귀뚜라미 소리 등 음향 기능을 더했다. 제품 출시 당시 방한한 테라오 겐(53)...

items.title: 빨래의 완성은 향기?
items.snippet: 갓 빤 수건에서는 기분 좋은 향이 난다. 햇볕에 말린 듯한 포근함에 은은한 꽃향기까지. 그런데 생각해 보면 이상하다. 깨끗한 빨래에는 왜 반드시 좋은 냄새가 나야 할까? 세탁의 목적은 때와 오염을 제거하는 것이지 향기를 입히는 것이 아닌데 말이다.

items.title: 산타도 놀라겠네, 크리스마스 케이크가 60만원
items.snippet: 크리스마스 케이크가 또다시 역대 최고가를 경신했다. 서울신라호텔이 크리스마스 시즌을 맞아 60만원짜리 ‘더 파이니스트 리저브’를 선보였다. 이 호텔에서 지난해 최고가였던 ‘더 파이니스트 럭셔리’(50만원)보다 10만원이 올랐다. 파티시에 3명이 화이트·블랙 트러플과 프랑스 디저트 와인 샤토 디켐 등 최고급 식재료를 사용해 하루 최대 3개 만든다.

items.title: 월급은 짧고 밤은 길다… 졸린 눈 부릅뜨는 ‘야간 경제’
items.snippet: 야경 너머에 누군가의 야근이 있다. 밤잠 물리치려는 몸부림, 편의점만 가 봐도 알 수 있다. 지난 1년간 심야 시간대(오후 10시~오전 4시) 국내 편의점에서 드러난 괄목할 변화는 ‘에너지 음료’와 ‘밥’ 판매 추이. 시장조사 기업 엠브레인 딥데이터에 따르면, 지난 6월 기준 에너지 음료 구매 건수는 약 733만건으로 지난해 같은 기간보다 41.5%, 밥류는 약 291만건으로 38.7% 급증했다. 야밤에 뇌를 깨우고 식량을 입에 밀어 넣는다. 힘써야 하므로.

items.title: AI가 하는 다이어트 조언 효과적일까
items.snippet: 점심으로 먹은 비빔밥 사진을 AI에 보여주면 몇 초 만에 열량을 알려준다. 달걀프라이 아래 깔린 고사리도 알아보고, 고추장을 조금 덜 넣으라는 조언까지 곁들인다. 내 몸에 맞는 음식을 골라 주기까지 한다. 팔에 연속혈당측정기(CGM)를 붙이고 대변으로 장내 미생물까지 분석해 정밀 맞춤 영양을 제공하는 기업이 국내외에서 주목받고 있다. AI로 무슨 일이든 할 수 있을 것 같은 세상이다. 사진, 혈당, 장내 미생물로 분석해 내놓는 AI의 조언은 얼마나 효과적일까?

items.title: 여우 본성 바꾼 실험… 과학은 이념보다 강했다
items.snippet: 1958년 구(舊)소련의 저명한 유전학자인 드미트리 벨랴예프(1917~1985)가 모스크바 국립대를 우등 졸업해 전도가 유망했던 젊은 동물생리학자 류드밀라 트루트(1933~2024)를 만났다. 벨랴예프는 그녀에게 대뜸 “여우를 개로 만들고 싶다”고 말했다. 온순한 여우끼리 교배시켜 늑대가 사람을 따르는 개가 된 과정을 재현하자는 황당한 제안이었다.

items.title: 이 추위에 야외에서 茶 마시는 사람들
items.snippet: 직장인 한모(33)씨는 주말이면 뜨거운 물이 든 보온병과 휴대용 1인 다기(茶器)를 들고 집 근처 공원으로 간다. 벤치에 작은 천을 깔고 찻잎을 우린 뒤, 1시간가량 여유롭게 차를 마신다. 한씨는 “기온이 떨어져 목도리까지 두르고 집을 나서지만 찬바람 맞으며 따뜻한 차를 마시면 머리가 맑아지고 기분도 한결 상쾌해진다”며 “차가운 공기 속에서 피어오르는 수증기와 찻잎의 향, 따뜻한 잔이 손에 전하는 온기 등 실내에서 경험하기 어려운 정취를 만끽할 수 있다”고 했다. 야외에서 다도를 즐기는 이들이 늘고 있다. ‘야차(野茶)’, ‘야다(야외 다도)’, ‘티크닉(차+피크닉)’이라고도 부른다. 한강공원 잔디밭이나 산, 바닷가 등에 자리를 잡고 직접 우려낸 차를 마시며 풍경을 감상하는 식이다.

items.title: 건물 한 층에 3700명분… 서울 한복판 친구집은 ‘대마 공장’이었다
items.snippet: 친구 사이인 A(29)씨와 B(29)씨는 지난해 1월부터 서울 성북구 주택가 건물 4층을 통째로 빌려 대마를 재배해 오다 적발돼 최근 중대범죄수사청에 구속됐다. 중수청은 현장에서 건조 대마 1.1㎏과 재배 중인 대마 33주를 압수했다. 3700명이 동시에 투약할 수 있는 분량이었다. C(33)씨는 지난해 3월부터 올 5월까지 서울 중랑구 자택에서 대마를 재배하다가 적발돼 징역 1년에 집행유예 2년을 선고받았다. 적발 당시 C씨가 보유한 대마는 587g으로, 1200명이 투약할 수 있는 분량이었다. C씨는 자기 집 1층 세탁실 뒤편과 2층 다락방에서 대마를 재배했다.

items.title: “네 개의 심장 소리 듣고 하나도 포기 할 수 없었죠”
items.snippet: 지난 18일 오전 11시 경기도 안양의 한 주거용 오피스텔 거실에 생후 15개월 된 네 쌍둥이 태이·채이·래이·재이가 함께 놀고 있었다. ‘태채래재 네 쌍둥이’로 불리는 이들 중 둘째 채이가 딸, 나머지 셋은 아들이다. 아이들은 거실을 기어다니다 서로 다리를 잡아보기도 하고, 한참 눈을 맞추기도 했다. 한 아이가 웃으면 다 같이 “까르르” 웃고, 한 아이가 손뼉 치면 다른 아이들도 따라 쳤다. 엄마 조세린(35)씨가 “이제 낮잠 잘 시간이야” 하자, 아빠 국은혁(36)씨가 아이들을 차례로 침대로 옮겼다. 처음엔 떼쓰던 아이들이 5분쯤 지나니 다 같이 잠이 들었다. 조씨는 “아이가 넷이라 자기들끼리 놀고, 잠도 침대에서 다 함께 잔다”고 했다.

items.title: Brightening spin- and parity-forbidden interlayer excitons through rhombohedral stacking
items.abstract: Brightened symmetry-forbidden excitons can provide critical information about the electronic structure and many-body interactions in semiconductors. Recently, interlayer atomic registry has emerged as a new way to control atomically thin layered materials in both ground and excited states. Here we show that the rhombohedral stacking in a 3R-MoS_2 homobilayer can brighten two symmetry-forbidden interlayer excitons: one is a spin-unlike 1s exciton and the other is a parity-odd 2p exciton. The nature of these interlayer excitons is revealed by their gfactors as well as the hybridization patterns observed when they are tuned to resonate with intralayer excitons. Surprisingly, the hybridized 2p exciton exhibits a constructive quantum interference between the acquired transition dipoles, revealing a hidden gauge-invariant phase contrast between the constituent electronic states. items.abstract: Charge noise from two-level fluctuators (TLFs) limits gate fidelities in semiconductor spin qubits, yet locating individual fluctuators within a device remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate a spatial triangulation method that combines the gate dependence of a TLF's detuning with the chemical potential shifts it induces in a sensing dot. Applying this method to previously reported measurements from a gated Si/SiGe quantum dot device, we use electrostatic simulations to jointly constrain the fluctuator's three-dimensional position and the magnitude of its electric dipole moment. items.abstract: Photonic N00N states enable phase sensing beyond the classical limit, but their generation conventionally relies on interferometric manipulation of photons using bulk optical components. Here we demonstrate the direct generation of a family of tunable two-photon polarization N00N states from a subwavelength-thick 3R-MoS2 flake. For propagation along the optic axis, the in-plane crystal symmetry allows all symmetry permitted spontaneous parametric down-conversion pathway to interfere coherently, while the large second-order nonlinearity provides sufficient brightness at submicrometer thickness without phase matching. The pump polarization sets the basis of the N00N state or equivalently a two-photon Holland-Burnett state without altering its structure or the generation efficiency. items.title: AFM metrology for 3D high aspect ratio semiconductor structures
items.abstract: Transistors have long been the foundation of the semiconductor industry, with continuous architectural innovations enabling the scaling of integrated circuits while maintaining high performance. Advancements in deposition and lithographic techniques have further expanded design possibilities, while increasing structural complexity demands stricter process control. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) offers a rapid and reliable metrology solution, providing high-resolution measurements and robust statistical analysis of critical parameters. In this work, we present clearly resolved individual profiles of lines and spaces in high aspect ratio (HAR) gate all around FET (GAAFET)-type structures on both the nanosheet (NS) region and in the isolation region between the nanosheets and we present a comprehensive statistical evaluation of their critical dimensions.

items.abstract: Scientific CMOS cameras are increasingly used in modern astronomy, offering CCD-like performance with lower power use, faster readout, and reduced cost. We evaluate the photometric precision of the Toran-26B camera, featuring the IMX571 sensor from Sony, a new CMOS camera from Andor Technology, through laboratory and on-sky tests in its two modes: high well capacity (HWC) and low noise (LN). Key metrics include read noise, dark current, photo and dark signal non-uniformity, quantum efficiency, and window transmittance. The median read noise is 1.07\,e$^-$ (LN) and 2.79\,e$^-$ (HWC). Bias shows minor dark signal non-uniformity: 0.076\,e$^-$ (LN), 0.173\,e$^-$ (HWC). Pixel well depth reaches 15700\,e$^-$ (LN) and 50000\,e$^-$ (HWC), with dynamic ranges of 83.39\,dB and 85.05\,dB, respectively. items.title: Real-Time Cryo-CMOS Photon-Number Readout from a Single SNSPD
items.abstract: Measurements leveraging the intrinsic photon-number resolution of Superconducting Nanostrip Single-Photon Detectors (SNSPDs) have recently gained traction due to the simplicity of the detector design. Intrinsic photon-number measurement schemes using SNSPDs encode the photon-number information in picosecond signal timing; these systems thus require high bandwidth readout and sensitive electrical measurement equipment. We show a cryogenic electronic circuit operating close to the SNSPD in the cryostat, which can isolate single-photon detection events directly from the SNSPD signal. This reduces the latency of the photon-number readout to (13.9 $\pm$ 0.3) ns, which enables feedforward operations based on intrinsic photon-number measurements with low latency.

items.title: Bayesian Calibration of Effective Material Parameters in Electric Machine Stators
items.abstract: Efficiency-driven faster switching by wide-bandgap semiconductor devices increases electromagnetic interference (EMI) in electric vehicles (EVs). Mitigating this EMI becomes more complex as system components grow. Therefore, electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) is assessed early via system-level simulation of the EV powertrain. A key EMC-critical quantity is the impedance of the electric drive machine, forming a major part of the EMI propagation path. Finite element (FE) simulations are typically used but are computationally expensive and limited by insufficient material property knowledge. We present a surrogate model based Bayesian calibration framework for 3D full-wave FE simulation of an externally excited synchronous motor (EESM) stator. items.abstract: High contact resistance, predominantly stemming from Fermi-level pinning (FLP), becomes a critical bottleneck in the contact engineering of transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) based two-dimensional field-effect transistors (2DFETs). Our study re-examines the inherent nature of FLP in 2D semiconductors, particularly focusing on regimes where the material thickness is commensurate with the interface thickness. Through the synergistic application of first-principles calculations and experimental validation via ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) and scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS), we rigorously establish the metal effective work function (eWF) as the definitive figure of merit for substantiating the Schottky-Mott relation. items.title: Carrier relaxation confines the Bogdanov--Takens degeneracy of an optically injected semiconductor laser
items.abstract: Optically injected semiconductor lasers are forced nonlinear oscillators whose locking boundaries are organized by codimension-two points. We ask which property of the carrier balance permits or forbids a Bogdanov--Takens (BT) point in the standard three-dimensional rate equations. Taking the carrier inversion $n$ as distinguished observable, the rate that enters the spectral conditions is the slope of the gain--loss balance, $ξ=\partial\dot n/\partial n=-2Γ/κ$, where $Γ$ is the damping of the relaxation oscillation and $κ=1+2Bn$ the normalized stimulated-emission factor. The two BT conditions become affine in $ξ$ and imply the exact sum rule $K^{2}=I[1-(1+κ)I]$ between injection amplitude $K$ and intracavity intensity $I$. items.title: From Entropy Source to Stochastic Bit-Stream: Low-Cost Converters for True-Random Stochastic Computing
items.abstract: Stochastic computing (SC) encodes values as the probability of ones in random bit-streams, which allows arithmetic circuits with very low area and power and a natural tolerance to faults. The accuracy and security of an SC system depend on the quality of those bit-streams. Conventional generators build them from pseudo-random or quasi-random sequences, which are predictable, periodic, and correlated across streams drawn from the same generator. This work proposes three methods for converting the unbiased outputs of a true random number generator (TRNG) into stochastic bit-streams (SBS) with arbitrary target probabilities: a block extraction and comparison circuit, a counter-logic circuit, and a cascaded majority-logic pipeline. items.title: A scalable dense silicon qubit architecture with logical operations
items.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) requires a large number of physical qubits to encode logical qubits with sufficiently low error rates. Silicon spin qubits are a promising platform because of their small footprint, compatibility with semiconductor manufacturing technologies, and demonstrated high-fidelity operations. However, realizing a scalable architecture that supports quantum error correction, qubit transport, wiring, and logical gate operations remains a major challenge. Here, we propose a scalable dense silicon spin qubit architecture designed to support large-scale FTQC. The architecture consists of qubit memories, data qubit lanes, and cross junctions. Qubit memories store logical qubits encoded using the rotated surface code and support logical single-qubit operations. Data qubit lanes enable high-speed one-dimensional spin shuttling for connectivity between logical qubi...

items.title: Low-barrier-height Hf$_\text{1-x}$Zr$_\text{x}$O$_2$ ferroelectric tunnel junctions with large ON-state currents
items.abstract: Ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) hold great promise for nonvolatile memory, neuromorphic computing, and other applications. Hf$_\text{1-x}$Zr$_\text{x}$O$_2$ (HZO) has become a leading candidate for the tunnel barrier due primarily to its compatibility with CMOS technology. Recent advances on HZO based FTJs have highlighted the importance of understanding the electrical transport through a ferroelectric tunnel barrier for fulfilling the technological promises of FTJs. In this paper we report investigation of HZO FTJs featuring a barrier of ultrathin HZO ($\leq$5nm) measured down to a temperature of 2 K. Direct quantum tunneling was found to dominate at low temperatures, along with contributions from trap-assisted tunneling. As the temperature increases, conduction by thermal activation takes over. items.title: Physics-Based TCAD Modeling of Nanowire Cryotrons with Coupled Superconducting and Thermal Dynamics
items.abstract: Nanowire cryotrons (nTrons) provide gate-controlled superconducting switching, current gain, and high-impedance outputs for cryogenic computing, detector readout, and superconductor-semiconductor interfaces. We develop a physics-based Sentaurus TCAD framework that couples time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau dynamics, separate electron and phonon energy equations, and mixed-mode circuit simulation. Superconducting terminal-current corrections connect the custom solver to the native electrical solution, linking local suppression of superconductivity, heating and cooling, and current redistribution in the external circuit. To our knowledge, this is the first Sentaurus-based mixed-mode TCAD implementation for nTrons. items.title: Unveiling ferroelectricity in wafer-scale beta-phase In$_2$Se$_3$
items.abstract: Pushing ferroelectricity to the ultimate thickness limit is a central challenge for memory hardware, because conventional three-dimensional ferroelectrics degrade through depolarization and interfacial effects when thinned. Here we identify $β$-In$_2$Se$_3$, a van der Waals semiconductor regarded as centrosymmetric, as a host of bistable polar order arising from a picometre-scale distortion within each quintuple layer. The polar state has out-of-plane and in-plane components, is switched by a vertical electric field, and persists to the bilayer limit (~1.9 nm) with an estimated coercive field of 0.9 MV/cm and an apparent remanent polarization of 11.0 $μ$C/cm$^2$. Films grown by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition on 2-inch wafers yield capacitor arrays with a switching-voltage spread below 5% across 100 devices, an endurance of $10^7$ cycles and a projected ten-year retention. items.abstract: A language-model decoder carries state between decoding steps, and in hardware a wrong state update can leave the current token correct and corrupt the output several tokens later, so a design can pass output tests and still be wrong. AIChipBench asks what LLM coding agents need to build such hardware correctly. Agents implement quantized Qwen3.5, Gemma 3, Gemma 4, and Llama 3.2 decoders in synthesizable register-transfer-level (RTL) code against an executable integer reference that specifies the outputs and the stored state at every decoding step. They debug against public tests under fixed budgets; their frozen designs are graded on held-out token sequences, resets, memory stalls, and synthesis, and a second track asks them to speed up a correct design at nearly fixed area. items.title: A library-based approach for inverse reconstruction of cavity depth using angle-resolved cathodoluminescence
items.abstract: In nanofabrication processes, accurate metrology is a crucial step for obtaining control over the required critical dimensions in a device. Traditionally, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is used to obtain high resolution measurements of the lateral dimension, but obtaining depth information on a thick sample is more complex. In this work, we use angle-resolved cathodoluminescence (AR-CL) spectroscopy to resolve this third dimension. Using 30 keV electrons in the SEM, CL is created at the bottom of a micrometer scale cavity milled in a gold surface. We show that reflections of the CL off the cavity sidewalls produce an interferogram which is a sensitive probe for the cavity geometry. items.title: Electron spin relaxation and coherence times of silicon vacancies in 4H-SiC
items.abstract: Color defect centers carrying electron spins in solid crystals like diamond and silicon carbide (SiC) are promising candidates for qubits and quantum sensors, with SiC material being particularly interesting due to its compatibility with the existing semiconductor technology. Here we investigated the electron spin properties of silicon vacancy centers (V1 and V2) both electron spin $S = 3/2$ in 4H-SiC in the temperature range $T=80-300$~K using electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR). The EPR spectrum shows central and satellite lines, where the former ones originate from V1 and V2 centers, as well as from unknown defect center X. The analysis of continuous wave EPR measurements revealed a spin concentration of $c_{\mathrm{V1}}=1.47\pm0.3\times10^{14}$, $c_{\mathrm{V2}}=5.6\pm1.12\times10^{13}$ and $c_{\mathrm{X}}=1.03\pm0.21\times10^{13}$ spins/cm$^{3}$. items.title: Design, Testing and Calibration of the GAPS Experiment Si(Li) Tracker Readout ASIC: From the First Flight Campaign Toward the Second Mission Upgrade
items.abstract: The General Antiparticle Spectrometer (GAPS) is a balloon-borne experiment designed to perform three long-duration flights from Antarctica to search for low-energy cosmic antinuclei, in particular antideuterons, as an indirect signature of dark matter. Its detection method relies on the formation and decay of exotic atoms, identified through the emission of characteristic x-rays and the subsequent annihilation into secondary particles. At the core of the instrument is the silicon tracker, composed of lithium-drifted silicon detectors operated at -40°C and read out by a custom application-specific integrated circuit, SLIDER32, implemented in 180 nm CMOS technology. This thesis reports on the integration, calibration, and validation of the SLIDER32-based tracker readout electronics. items.title: Certified minimax normal-scale mixtures for the logistic-normal integral
items.abstract: The logistic distribution function is a scale mixture of normal distribution functions, and Monahan and Stefanski approximate it by the $K$-term mixture $Λ(x) \approx \sum_{i} w_i Φ(s_i x)$ chosen to minimise the uniform error on the real line. Each such mixture reduces the logistic-normal integral to a sum of $K$ normal distribution functions with the mixture's uniform error bound. This integral is the expectation of a logistic sigmoid over a normal distribution in statistics and the Gauss-Fermi integral in semiconductor physics. Monahan and Stefanski tabulate constants for $K \le 8$ and conjecture that the optimal error equioscillates at $2K$ points, while above $K = 8$ the Remez exchange and local solvers stall at nonequioscillating stationary points. items.title: First-principles phase diagram of monolayer CrS$_2$ polymorphs under biaxial strain and its sensitivity to the Hubbard U parameter
items.abstract: In correlated two-dimensional magnets the balance between competing electronic and magnetic phases is often set by the strength of the on-site Coulomb interaction, so that the predicted ground state can hinge on a parameter that is not uniquely defined. Monolayer CrS$_2$ lies squarely in this regime, hosting several energetically close polymorphs whose character ranges from non-magnetic semiconducting to magnetically ordered metallic. We therefore investigate, using DFT$+U$ within the generalized gradient approximation, the structural, magnetic, and electronic properties of the 1H, 1T, 1T$'$, and 1T$''$ polymorphs of monolayer CrS$_2$ under varying Hubbard interactions ($U=0$--$8$~eV) and biaxial strain ($-10\%$ to $+10\%$). items.title: N-Polar AlGaN/GaN Heterojunction Bipolar Transistor
items.abstract: Heterojunction bipolar transistors based on the III-Nitride systems have significantly lower performance than field effect transistors due to challenges associated with p-type doping of the base. N-polar AlGaN/GaN HBTs can overcome these challenges by polarization-induced holes in the base and base-emitter interface. We experimentally demonstrate the first N-polar AlGaN/GaN heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) grown by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy on GaN substrate without emitter regrowth. The HBTs exhibit a peak current gain of approximately 15, peak differential current gain of approximately 18, and emitter-area-normalized peak current densities exceeding 20 kA/cm^2 and 66 kA/cm^2 for emitter areas of 10 x 10 um^2 and 3 x 10 um^2, respectively. items.title: Real-Time AI Acceleration on a 2D Spatial Dataflow Architecture
items.abstract: Machine Learning (ML) is increasingly being integrated into real-time systems, which makes the timing analysis of ML accelerators necessary. However, the most popular commercial accelerator, the Graphics Processing Unit (GPU), remains difficult to analyze as several aspects of its behavior, including scheduling of threads involved in single-instruction multiple-thread computations and memory access latency, are not fully documented. Spatial dataflow accelerators present an interesting alternative to GPUs, as they inherently support compute and memory partitioning. Data movement and computation locality are explicitly controlled by the programmer. In this work, we consider the Tenstorrent Blackhole, which is based on a commodity RISC-V architecture. items.title: Neural-operator acceleration of bidirectional phonon Boltzmann-Fourier coupling for multiscale heat transport in silicon fin arrays
items.abstract: Localized heating in semiconductor devices can produce non-diffusive phonon transport near heat-generating regions, while heat spreading through the surrounding substrate remains well described by Fourier conduction. We present a hybrid framework that couples a pretrained neural operator for the phonon Boltzmann transport equation (BTE) within individual fins to a Fourier model of a shared substrate. To reduce the cost of repeated BTE solves across fin positions and coupling iterations, a DeepONet maps each fin's substrate-interface temperature and heating state to its temperature and heat-flux fields. The operator is trained on interface temperatures generated by a linearized proxy of the coupled problem, which avoids explicit training data collection from full coupled runs. items.title: Resilience of Entangling Gates to Spatiotemporally Correlated Noise
items.abstract: As quantum processors scale, spatially and temporally correlated noise is emerging as a limiting factor in the fidelity of multiqubit gates. Here we show that this makes the choice of entangling operation a first-order design decision: for two-qubit gates in semiconductor spin qubits, the CZ and $\sqrt{\mathrm{iSWAP}}$ gates exhibit a pronounced resilience to correlated noise relative to the SWAP gate, even though correlated fluctuations of the entangling interaction can degrade gate performance to a level comparable to that of local noise. items.title: Generalized dielectric-dependent hybrid functional combining Gaussian and Yukawa screening
items.abstract: We develop a generalized Coulomb-attenuated method (GCAM) for dielectric-dependent hybrid functionals that combines Gaussian and Yukawa-type screening functions to provide an accurate representation of the random-phase approximation (RPA) dielectric function. Through systematic fitting to RPA dielectric functions of semiconductors and insulators, and to the Lindhard dielectric function of the homogeneous electron gas, we demonstrate that GCAM significantly reduces errors in the model dielectric function across the full momentum range. However, despite this improved physical description of screening, band gap calculations reveal that GCAM yields larger errors compared to experiment than previous CAM approaches for wide-gap materials, but smaller errors for most narrow-gap materials. This counterintuitive result demonstrates that the success of CAM stems not purely from physical reasons, b...

items.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors offer a viable platform for next-generation electronics beyond sub-3 nm nodes, yet essential nonlinear circuit elements, such as thyristors, remain unexplored on atomically thin platforms. Here, we report an atomically thin reconfigurable electro-optical thyristor based on a lateral WSe2-MoSe2-WSe2-MoSe2 PNPN heterostructure, directly grown via sequential edge epitaxy. Unlike single-junction 2D diodes, this multijunction architecture exhibits thyristor-like nonlinear switching, including forward blocking, abrupt snapback, bistability, and electrical latching. The device exhibits a forward-blocking voltage of 183 V, corresponding to a critical electric field of 1 MV/cm. items.abstract: Metal-Insulator-Metal (MIM) plasmonic refractive index (RI) sensors have attracted considerable attention for label-free, real-time analyte detection; however, their reliance on noble metals such as gold and silver imposes fundamental constraints on tunability, thermal stability, and CMOS process compatibility. items.title: Scanning nanowire quantum dot with radio-frequency read-out
items.abstract: Scanning single-electron transistors (SETs) are highly sensitive local probes of charge and electric potential, but their integration with robust height control for scanning probe microscopy remains challenging. Furthermore, readout bandwidths are limited to tens of kHz, while characterizing faster charge dynamics is often of interest. Here, we present a scanning SET in the form of a nanowire (NW) quantum dot (QD) integrated at the apex of a non-contact atomic force microscopy (NC-AFM) cantilever. We demonstrate NC-AFM topographic imaging and local electrometry capability by mapping the electrostatic potential generated by a set of nanoscale voltage-biased gate electrodes. Comparison with electrostatic simulations shows agreement with the measured potential profiles. items.abstract: Centimetre-sized meteoroids released by the active asteroid (3200) Phaethon, parent of the Geminid meteor shower, probe the ejection of refractory material from a comet-asteroid transition object and the age of the stream; lunar impact flashes (LIFs) are the only ground-based technique that samples this size range. We determine the impact flux, mass and size distributions, and expected crater sizes of Geminid meteoroids on the Moon from campaigns at the 2018 and 2025 maxima, and test the stability of the centimetre-sized population over seven years. Both campaigns used the Nihon University 0.40 m "GUNDAM" telescope with CMOS video cameras at 60 fps, with candidates validated at independent stations; a common aperture-photometry pipeline calibrated in the Cousins R band gave peak magnitudes to 0.1-0.25 mag. items.title: Anatomy of orbital and spin responses in GaAs and Si: Hall, inverse Faraday, and magneto-optical Kerr effects
items.abstract: Magneto-optical signals in nonmagnetic semiconductors entangle spin and orbital contributions, both in angular-momentum generation and magneto-optical detection. We calculate these contributions for electron-doped GaAs and Si using density-functional theory, linear-response theory, and a second-order density-matrix treatment of the inverse Faraday effect. At small electron doping, the intrinsic orbital Hall conductivity exceeds its spin counterpart in magnitude, while the orbital contribution to light-induced magnetization dominates over broad photon-energy ranges. We show that orbital- and spin-resolved optical Hall and polar Kerr coefficients exhibit stronger sensitivity to orbital moments than to equal spin moments. items.title: Numerical simulations of CCP-2D GEC with sGMRES
items.abstract: Fluid models provide an efficient means of simulating the low-temperature gas discharges, which are important in semiconductor manufacturing. This work presents, to the best of our knowledge, the first systematic numerical framework for the Gaseous Electronics Conference (GEC) reference cell of the 2D capacitively coupled plasma (CCP). The framework employs a structured, nonuniform cylindrical mesh to resolve the spatial gradients. A semi-implicit Scharfetter-Gummel (SG) scheme is used for the Poisson's equation, while the implicit SG schemes are applied to the continuity equations and the electron energy equation. Both the explicit and and the implicit formulations based on the conventional drift-diffusion terms are also investigated. To solve the resulting large-scale linear systems, we introduce an incomplete LU (ILU)-preconditioned sketched GMRES (sGMRES) method as the solver. As far...

items.abstract: Terahertz (THz) technology has witnessed notable developments in sensing, spectroscopy, imaging, and wireless communication which have increased the demand for high-performance THz modulators. Among the various approaches for controlling the THz waves, the application of external stimuli such as optical pumping and thermal or electric fields is widely employed as a promising strategy for modulation. This review focuses on recent advances in THz modulation based on different materials including 2D semiconductors and metamaterials with attention to their response under external stimuli. items.title: Indentation-induced polar domain reconfiguration in the charge-density-wave semiconductor EuTe4
items.abstract: Controlling polar domains in conducting materials by external fields could unlock polarization-based electronic functionalities, yet remains experimentally challenging. While mechanical actuation driven by local strain, stress, or strain gradients has been proposed as an external-voltage-free route, its experimental demonstration in relatively conducting polar materials remains limited. Here we demonstrate mechanically induced polar-domain reconfiguration in the charge-density-wave (CDW) semiconductor EuTe4 at room temperature, whose resistivity is on the order of 10 m$Ω$cm. Polarized-light microscopy and second-harmonic-generation measurements reveal CDW-induced in-plane polarization domains with an approximately 90 $^\circ$ domain configuration. items.title: Proposal for a cat-cluster-state machine gun
items.abstract: Non-Gaussian bosonic states such as the Schrödinger cat states are essential for continuous-variable quantum-information processing. A convenient and deterministic process for generating cat states is through the use of a Rabi interaction between a single bosonic mode and a spin which facilitates a state-dependent displacement. The lack of a Rabi interaction for propagating optical photons has rendered optical cat states elusive. Here, we show that the complex nonlinear scattering dynamics of a single-mode squeezed-vacuum state interacting with a quantum emitter can be engineered to produce a Rabi interaction between a quantum emitter and a propagating photon mode while the contributions from other orthogonal modes destructively interfere. items.title: Population of spin orbit-split-electron branches in semimetallic HgTe quantum wells
items.abstract: We present the results of experimental studies on magnetoresistance, the Hall effect, and Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations performed in gated heterostructures with HgTe-based gapless semiconductor quantum wells. We show that in quantum wells with widths corresponding to a semimetallic charge carrier spectrum, electrons, in contrast to the idealized model, populate both spin-orbit-split branches of the spectrum. This occurs regardless of whether the Fermi level lies exclusively in the conduction band or within the conduction-valence band overlap region.

items.title: AgenticMM: A Material-Centered Multi-Agent Architecture for Scalable First-Principles Materials Modeling
items.abstract: Multi-agent frameworks are attracting increasing attention as a means of autonomously driving complex, long-running workflows in first-principles materials modeling. However, such frameworks commonly organize AI agents by computational task or scientific role. When scaled across many materials, this organization can require repeated transfers of material-specific context and complicate persistent execution and resource coordination. Here, we introduce AgenticMM, a material-centered multi-agent architecture in which each material has a persistent agent that owns its complete workflow and retains its scientific context, while a persistent coordinator allocates shared resources, mediates communication, and tracks campaign progress. items.title: JAX-Nano: A GPU-Accelerated Differentiable Phonon Boltzmann Transport Solver for Nanoscale Heat Transfer
items.abstract: As semiconductor device dimensions approach phonon mean free paths, heat transport enters ballistic and quasi-ballistic regimes where Fourier's law becomes inadequate. The phonon Boltzmann transport equation (BTE) describes these nonequilibrium effects but presents significant computational challenges. This work introduces JAX-Nano, a GPU-accelerated, end-to-end differentiable phonon BTE solver for nanoscale heat transport. The solver integrates steady-state and transient BTE formulations within a unified finite-volume framework, supporting structured and unstructured meshes, mode-resolved transport, phonon scattering, volumetric heat generation, and multiple boundary conditions. Automatic differentiation enables gradient computation with respect to transport properties, boundary conditions, heat-generation rates, and geometric parameters without separately derived adjoint equations. items.title: Learning in the Passive Space: End-to-End Muti-Order Port-Hamiltonian Macromodeling
items.abstract: Compact, passive state-space macromodels of interconnects and power-delivery networks are essential for stable transient signal- and power-integrity simulations. However, conventional flows require costly per-layout full-wave electromagnetic (EM) simulations, while both traditional fitting and prior learning surrogates rely on post-hoc fitting or passivity perturbation that degrades accuracy without guaranteeing convergence. items.title: Single-Photon Detectors for Optical Wireless Communications: A Tutorial
items.abstract: Photon-counting receivers extend optical wireless communication (OWC) into regimes in which only a few detected photons are available per information bit, but the detector can no longer be treated as an interchangeable ideal counter. This tutorial develops a communication-oriented, port-to-bit framework for single-photon detection in indoor, terrestrial, airborne, space, underwater, non-line-of-sight, and integrated communication-and-sensing links. It compares SPADs, silicon photomultipliers, CMOS SPAD arrays, superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors, PMT/MCP-PMT receivers, upconversion detectors, and emerging technologies through photon-detection efficiency, timing, active area, dynamic range, spectral coverage, readout, cooling, and integration requirements. items.title: First-Principles Investigation of the {ScSe2} TMDs Monolayer: Structural Stability, Electronic and Optical Properties
items.abstract: We present an ab initio investigation of the {ScSe2} monolayer using density functional theory (DFT), as employed in the CP2K code, to assess its structural stability and electronic properties. The electronic behavior of both phases is governed by the local coordination environment of scandium and the associated lifting of degeneracy of its $3d$ orbitals. The valence bands (VBs) are dominated by {Se}$-4p$ states in both phases, while the states near the Fermi level distinguish the metallic 1T phase from the semiconducting 2H phase. Optical response calculations reveal markedly different spectral signatures for the two polymorphs. Two findings emerge from this study: a polymorphism-driven metal-to-semiconductor transition without any change in chemical composition and distinct optical responses relevant to phase-selective optoelectronic devices.

items.title: CHARMS250V1: A Cryogenic Front-End ASIC for Low-Noise Readout of Charge or Light Signals in Noble Liquid Detectors
items.abstract: This work presents the design and measurement results of CHARMS250V1, a next-generation cryogenic front-end application specific integrated circuit (ASIC) developed using a 65 nm CMOS process. It is designed for low-noise readout of charge or light signals generated in noble liquid detectors. CHARMS250V1 is a single channel prototype whose design in the future will be integrated within a 16-channel ASIC. It comprises pre-amplification and pulse shaping stages that provide programmable charge gain between 4.3 mV/fC and 25 mV/fC, peaking time programmable between 250 ns and 2 us, and programmable baseline of either 200 mV or 900 mV for processing of unipolar and bipolar signals, respectively.

items.title: Metal to Semiconductor Transition in Niobium Sulfoselenide Alloy Films by Compositional Control
items.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have garnered significant interest due to their tunable bandgaps, optical anisotropy, and mechanical flexibility. This study explores the relationship between stoichiometry, structural phase, and electronic transport in niobium sulfoselenide (NbSxSe2-x) thin films. In this study, low-dimensional TMD films were grown with molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) to investigate the effects of varying chalcogen (sulfur and selenium) content in NbSxSe2-x alloys. We focus on tuning electrical resistivity along with the transition from metallic-to-semiconducting behavior through compositional control. These MBE grown films were characterized using in-vacuo x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) to analyze the chemical composition. items.title: Optical Scintillation Imaging for Dynamic Source Tracking Dosimetry During Prostate HDR Brachytherapy
items.abstract: High-dose-rate (HDR) brachytherapy is highly conformal, but its accuracy depends on catheter and source placement, and clinical workflows lack real-time in vivo dosimetry (IVD) that verifies delivery without disrupting the procedure. We characterize a scintillator-based optical dosimeter integrated into a transrectal probe that tracks source position, speed, dose rate, and time-resolved cumulative dose. A 67 mm x 5 mm line scintillator is imaged by a CMOS camera through a 30-degree endoscopic lens; geometric and flat-field corrections remove barrel distortion and vignetting. Absolute dose was calibrated with a TOPAS Monte Carlo model of the probe's air-cavity geometry. The system was validated in a water phantom with an Ir-192 source and needles at radial offsets of 7, 10, and 15 mm. items.title: Physical Learning for Autonomous Tuning of Spin Qubits in Electrostatically Defined Quantum Dots
items.abstract: Tuning electrostatically defined quantum dots remains a primary bottleneck in the scalability of semiconductor spin qubits. While existing solutions rely on machine learning algorithms, these approaches require global information, introduce latency bottlenecks, and tax the limited cooling power available at cryogenic stages. Here, we demonstrate an FPGA-in-the-loop learning paradigm that bypasses digital computing overhead by utilizing multiplexed gradient descent (MGD) for tuning. Implemented on an FPGA and an emulated quantum dot device, our system autonomously tracks environmental drift, dynamically recovers from discrete charge jumps, and maintains steady-state stabilization in low signal-to-noise ratio regimes, without prior knowledge of the device's cross-capacitance matrix. items.title: Coherence Lengths of Laser Pointers
items.abstract: We report on the coherence lengths of low-cost green laser pointers in the midst of multimodal behavior using an optical interferometer based on noncollinear beam geometries and a CMOS detector array. Examined devices include three diode lasers and a frequency-doubled neodymium-emission diode-pumped solid state (DPSS) laser. Coherence length measurements are variable among devices, but values can nevertheless regularly exceed 10 cm. The work serves as a template for an advanced undergraduate physics laboratory experiment and may inspire new kinds of laser pointer devices utilizing interference effects as operative principles.

items.abstract: Closing the final 5%-15% of code and functional coverage remains a major schedule bottleneck in silicon tapeouts. Existing LLM-based coverage closure loops feed raw uncovered RTL lines or branches directly into iterative prompts, failing on industrial subsystems due to: (1) token and context explosion from querying thousands of correlated holes independently; (2) illegal stimulus that violates cross-signal invariants and yields dirty coverage; and (3) unsafe exclusion hallucination on structurally unreachable dead code. We present ARGUS (Autonomous Reachability & Guided Unified Stimulus), a specification-grounded, dual-regime coverage closure and formal exclusion synthesis engine. items.title: Magnon high-harmonic generation by nonlinearities of spin torque driven by phonon-mediated crossing of many-body energy levels of bright and dark excitons
items.abstract: Recent intense experimental focus on CrSBr, a two-dimensional (2D) antiferromagnetic semiconductor, has revealed numerous surprises in its response to ultrafast optical drive. We demonstrate that a single microscopic mechanism accounts for two of them---high-harmonic generation of magnons and persistence of magnon oscillations over \mbox{$\sim 1$ ns} time scale that is much longer than the femtosecond laser pulse (fsLP) pump duration. This mechanism arises from an unusually complex interplay of four different fundamental quasiparticles of condensed matter physics: magnons, optically bright and dark excitons, and phonons. By viewing magnons as the system and the other three quasiparticles as a quantum many-body bath, we derive an extended Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (eLLG) equation. Its new term generated by the bath is spatially nonlocal and time-dependent, as well as strongly {\em nonlinear...

items.title: From power to spectrum: an off-the-shelf photodiode turned into a spectrometer by its bias alone
items.abstract: Computational spectrometers replace dispersive optics with detectors whose spectral response can be varied, but every reported single-detector device obtains this response through dedicated fabrication: two-dimensional heterostructures, graded epitaxial junctions, organic stacks, filters or photonic circuits. We demonstrate a generic, fabrication-free alternative in which a standard commercial photodiode becomes a spectrometer through its electrical drive alone, requiring no modification of the device, no optical filter and no modulation of the light. The mechanism is bias-modulated optoelectronic chromatic dispersion (OED): light of different wavelengths is absorbed at different depths, and a sinusoidal bias changes how carriers generated at each depth are collected, so that every spectrum is encoded in the shape of the photocurrent waveform over one bias period. items.abstract: A fundamental property of interlayer excitons is their dipolar character, enabling electrical tunability, enhanced exciton-exciton interactions and extended lifetime. It is important for studying collective phenomena and realizing novel optoelectronic devices. However, in homo- or heterostructures based on two-dimensional semiconductors, the magnitude and orientation of the dipole moment are commonly locked due to spatially confined charges and nature of the band transition. Here, we use gate-dependent photoluminescence of few-layer R-WSe2 to harness sliding ferroelectricity for controlling the exciton dipole configuration of emerging layer-hybridised excitons. The sliding-ferroelectric control enables a pronounced on/off switching of the diffusive transport of hybrid dipolar excitons, while further facilitating gradual and abrupt dipole reconfigurations with emerging quadrupolar exciton...

items.title: Topology-Enabled Self-Verification of Quantum Hall Resistance Standards
items.abstract: The scaling of multi-element quantized Hall array resistance standards necessitates rigorous validation that internal quantization has not broken down without relying on the verification of dissipationless edge state transport. One proposed solution is to use a Symmetric Precision Quantization Reliability criterion, a mathematical framework that statistically assures such validation strictly through outer terminal measurements of Cn-symmetric designs. This criterion essentially bounds the likelihood of hidden localized defects arising from quantum Hall breakdown and has potential uses in quantum computing and semiconductor testing but is presented in the context of its application toward quantum electrical standards.

items.title: Thermal investigation of buffer and transition layers in AlGaN HEMT stacks
items.abstract: In this work, we investigate thermal transport in a set of thin-film layers used in modern HEMT designs. Our theoretical analysis employs three phonon-transport models of increasing sophistication, ranging from a relatively simple Debye-approximation model to a first-principles framework that incorporates Density Functional Theory (DFT)-derived harmonic and anharmonic phonon properties. To describe ternary semiconductors, alloy scattering is also considered, and to account for the properties of non-ideal, polycrystalline thin films, scattering at grain and film boundaries is taken into account. For modeling the specific samples at hand, the latter are fitted to thermal conductivity data measured with Time-Domain Thermoreflectance (TDTR). Overall, we find that the first-principles model performs best and produces the most physically consistent results. Special emphasis is placed on establ...

items.title: CRAFT: Analog Circuit Design by Reasoning LLM Agents from Pre-Computed Lookup Tables
items.abstract: Automated analog circuit sizing methods, from black-box optimizers to recent large language model (LLM) agents, typically search the design space with a SPICE simulator in the loop, whereas an experienced designer works out a design by hand analysis. This paper presents CRAFT, a flow in which an LLM agent designs a given topology by calculation, as a designer does, and without an initial sizing. The agent works only through DeX, a service that uses pre-computed lookup tables to provide device characteristics and to solve the whole netlist for its operating point and small-signal response. It thus designs without SPICE, and every final design is verified independently in HSPICE. We test CRAFT on four circuits in a commercial 28 nm process; the largest is a 37-transistor three-stage amplifier with 53 design variables, 20 specifications and 74 saturation constraints. items.abstract: Embodied agents are emerging as a promising paradigm for complex robotic tasks, leveraging Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and World Action Models (WAMs) to generate actions through Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-based iterative denoising. However, existing models often struggle to generalize to out-of-distribution (OOD) environments. We observe that retrieving successful experiences and using them to warm-start denoising enables agents to better adapt to unfamiliar situations while reducing computational overhead. This creates a new opportunity to improve task accuracy and inference efficiency simultaneously, in contrast to conventional acceleration techniques that trade accuracy for computation. items.title: Origin and hole-density dependence of the intrinsic spin Hall conductivity in inorganic halide perovskites
items.abstract: Metal halide perovskites have spin-orbit coupling among the strongest in semiconductors, yet whether their centrosymmetric bulk phases can convert charge current into spin current, and what controls the response, is unknown. Here we identify, from first-principles calculations on the four all-inorganic compounds CsBX3 (B = Pb, Sn; X = Br, I), the factors that govern their intrinsic spin Hall conductivity. The conductivity arises from the spin Berry curvature of the spin-orbit-split halide-p bands, 1.1-2.6 eV below the valence band maximum, and exceeds that of III-V and group-IV semiconductors when the Fermi level lies inside them. Because the valence band maximum is an s-p singlet, shifted only in second order, these contributions cancel in the undoped compounds, which respond like conventional semiconductors. With hole doping the response recovers, and at densities reachable by electric...

items.title: Interfacing Silicon Nitride Nanophotonics with Cuprous Oxide Rydberg Excitons
items.abstract: Rydberg excitons in cuprous oxide (Cu$_2$O), the solid-state counterpart of Rydberg atoms, are hydrogen-like electron--hole quasi-particles with micron-sized wavefunctions and strong long-range interactions that promise optical nonlinearities at the few-photon level. Exploiting them in a waveguide quantum electrodynamics (WQED) setting can enable what atomic Rydberg platforms achieve only with ultrahigh vacuum and laser cooling/trapping---a guided optical mode interfaced with the Rydberg medium---while adding the scalability and advanced fabrication of integrated photonics. Here we demonstrate a monolithic, CMOS-compatible interface of Cu$_2$O Rydberg excitons with a SiN$_x$ nanophotonic waveguide. items.title: Design and Modeling of Graded Base III-Nitride HBTs for High-Frequency Applications
items.abstract: This work analyzes the high-frequency performance constraints of AlGaN/GaN heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) and proposes a novel band-engineered graded base N-polar AlGaN/GaN HBT and evaluates the RF performances. Unlike conventional p-GaN base designs, we propose a graded base in the N-polar orientation which offers polarization-induced hole accumulation with quasi-electric field-assisted minority carrier transport. The proposed design simultaneously mitigates the longstanding current crowding, Webster effect, and conventional base resistance limitations. Using well-calibrated two-dimensional TCAD simulations, the proposed compositionally graded base HBT projects peak f_T/f_{MAX} of 190/200 GHz with a power density (V_{BR}I_{MAX}/8 > 20 W/mm), offering a promising pathway toward simultaneous high-frequency and high-power GaN millimeter-wave electronics.

We study their electronic properties by a combination of scanning tunneling spectroscopy and density functional theory, revealing the intricate influences of geometry, underlying point group symmetries and spin-orbit coupling on hybridized states. items.title: Optical readout of MicroPattern Gaseous Detectors with SiPMs
items.abstract: Scintillation light readout of MicroPattern Gaseous Detectors (MPGDs) is used for imaging and track reconstruction applications including in optical Time Projection Chambers (TPC). Typically, high resolution CCD or CMOS imaging sensors are used and PMTs can be employed to obtain auxiliary timing information. We report on the optical readout of MPGDs with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs) which enables limited spatial resolution. Arrays of SiPMs were used to read out Gaseous Electron Multipliers (GEMs) and Glass Micromegas amplification stages. Center of gravity reconstruction of hit positions yields a spatial resolution of approximately 1.35 mm for signals shared across multiple SiPMs. High gain of the amplification stage as well as the SiPMs enables good signal sharing and is advantageous for position reconstruction.

items.title: Reliable arithmetic circuits using less reliable (sub-digital) logic
items.abstract: The frequent static failure of CMOS logic gates at ultra-low voltages has historically been perceived as a strict barrier to extreme voltage scaling: this paper introduces a statistical circuit law proving this intuition wrong. We discovered a universal power law connecting gate and circuit static failure probabilities, revealing that circuit failure requires the simultaneous breakdown of an entire gate cluster rather than a single component. Because the required cluster size increases rapidly as voltage drops, low-voltage \textit{sub-digital} logic exhibits surprising inherent resilience to static failure. This insight stems from new theoretical tools we developed to quantify static failure, extending well beyond conventional voltage-margin analysis. Consequently, sub-digital processors could potentially offer a viable, near-term solution to drastically reduce the energy demands of AI.

The inverse of the delay mismatch between each pair of lasers introduces characteristic frequencies that shape the spectral response of the synchronized system. By studying two different three-laser configurations, we find that peaks appear whenever multiple harmonic contributions overlap in frequency, resulting in constructive enhancement of the spectral power. items.title: Ultrafast Successive Control and Electrical Detection of Long-Lived Valley Polarization in Room-Temperature Germanium
items.abstract: Germanium (Ge) hosts four degenerate valleys in the conduction band minima, and their highly anisotropic effective masses offer a valley degree of freedom in transport phenomena via anisotropic conductivity. Using time- and polarization-resolved terahertz spectroscopy combined with deformation potential theory, we reveal a valley relaxation time reaching 10 ps near the band edge of Ge(001) at room temperature, long enough to detect the valley polarization in electrical transport measurements. We also demonstrate sub-picosecond complete reversal of valley polarization by off-resonant light pulses at extremely low energy consumption. These results pave the way for room-temperature valleytronics based on bulk indirect-gap semiconductors compatible with existing electronics.

items.title: Fault-tolerant quantum processor with minimal external control
items.abstract: Contemporary classical information processors integrate tens of billions of transistors printed on a chip, yet are fully controlled through comparatively few external wires. This is possible because data flows through hard-coded operations in step with a global clock and is steered by external instructions. Today's solid-state quantum processors are different -- every qubit receives instructions from outside the chip via its own dedicated control line, and error correction adds a further torrent of syndrome data that is transported off-chip. Here we show that the external control of a quantum chip can be greatly simplified. We propose a fault-tolerant architecture for universal quantum computation, inspired by modern classical processors, in which quantum information flows through a fixed, clocked device, propelled by local gates in a planar array. Tuning spreading transport in GaN HEMTs with an AlN space layer under non-equilibrium heating
items.abstract: Lateral spreading transport dominates near-junction heat dissipation in GaN high-electron-mobility transistors, yet thermal control has largely overlooked this geometry. It neither reaches the core AlGaN/GaN region nor, beyond the spatial spreading itself, accounts for the spectral non-equilibrium of the heat source. Here we tune the spreading resistance directly by inserting a thin, highly conducting AlN space layer above the source to intercept heat and divert it laterally. We test this approach across GaN, AlGaN/GaN, and AlGaN/AlN/GaN structures under both equilibrium and longitudinal-optical (LO)-pumped non-equilibrium heating, pairing non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (NEMD) with full-band phonon Monte Carlo (MC). items.title: Breaking the Myth of Four-Tier Stacked Transistors for Logic: an Investigation from Process to Device and Block-Level PPA
items.abstract: For the first time, this work evaluated whether 4-tier stacked transistors can translate the straightforward density gains into realistic chip-level scaling benefits. A practical dual-sided 4-tier transistor-stacking CFFET (Flipped CFET-to-CFET) process was proposed, on which a DTCO framework spanning standard-cell design, local interconnects, RO analysis, and physical implementation was built under 2A node design rules. The CFFET was also benchmarked with its 2-tier transistor-stacking counterparts FFET. Among CFFET configurations, the best-performing Symmetric Power still lags FFET by 11.2% in RO frequency due to the complex MOL parasitics. At the block level, CFFET reduces the Ibex RISC-V core area by only 12.8% (far below the 40% nominal cell-height reduction), while running 10.9% slower at iso-power. items.title: A Probabilistic Behavioral RTL Simulation Framework for Probabilistic Compute Fabrics
items.abstract: Coupled oscillator Ising hardware can produce different solution qualities across repeated runs of the same problem, while a deterministic behavioral model used for the design yields a single outcome under fixed conditions. Capturing this stochastic variability during design time is essential for evaluating how closely simulation reflects silicon behavior. This work presents a probabilistic behavioral RTL simulation framework that introduces Gaussian timing variation into coupling delays. This variation changes oscillator timing during evolution, producing different outcomes across runs while retaining the existing chip control and readout blocks. The framework is evaluated against measurements from two chips: a 28-nm CMOS chip with 66 spins and a 16-nm FinFET chip with 49 spins, using 250 problems run 100 times repetitively. items.abstract: This work presents a novel computer-aided design (CAD) tool for gradient-based circuit optimization using SPICE and automatic differentiation, which we term ADSPICE. Automatic differentiation (AD) is a technique for evaluating a derivative by breaking it into its elementary differentiation operations and repeatedly applying the chain rule, in contrast with a finite-difference-based derivative computed from a small perturbation. Native SPICE (realized with ngspice) is equipped with automatic differentiation toward gradient-based optimization, particularly adjoint-mode optimization. This is implemented with custom C code and shared library control, allowing easy integration with existing SPICE infrastructure. Despite their improved electrostatic control, recent measurements show that the drain current in GAAFETs deviates strongly from thermionic behavior at negative gate voltages, increasing as the gate voltage becomes more negative. This leakage has been attributed to direct gate-drain tunneling through the high-$k$ dielectric, enhanced by drain-induced dielectric barrier lowering (DIDBL). Here, we use predictive, charge-self-consistent Non-Equilibrium Green Function (NEGF) simulations based on the Contact Block Reduction (CBR) method to spatially resolve this leakage pathway in GAAFETs. items.title: BROAD: Bit-Parallel Row-Oriented Arithmetic in DRAM
items.abstract: Processing-using-memory (PUM) architectures perform computation directly within DRAM to reduce costly data movement between memory and processors. Because charge-sharing operations are confined to individual bitlines, existing DRAM-PUM architectures reorganize data into column-oriented, bit-serial representations. This organization is fundamentally incompatible with the row-oriented, word-parallel layouts used by conventional processors and accelerators, requiring expensive data-layout transformations whenever computation transitions between PUM and conventional execution. In this paper, we present BROAD, or Bit-Parallel Row-Oriented Arithmetic in DRAM. BROAD augments the DRAM subarray with two lightweight extensions: migration cells that enable localized horizontal data movement between neighboring bitlines and inversion cells that provide efficient in-array logical inversion. items.title: SPLASH: Co-Designing Flash-Aware Sparse Attention with a Virtualized HBM-HBF Hierarchy
items.abstract: As context lengths, request lifetimes and concurrency grow, the key-value (KV) cache dominates memory usage in large language model (LLM) inference. High-bandwidth memory (HBM), the memory on contemporary GPUs, achieves far higher bandwidth than off-package memory, yet its capacity, bounded by DRAM density, has not kept pace with this demand. High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF), an emerging memory technology, bridges this gap, combining the advanced packaging of HBM with the density of flash to deliver terabyte-scale capacity at HBM-class read bandwidth. Exploiting this capacity for long-context KV caches, however, requires hiding the vastly different physical characteristics of flash from the GPU while keeping decode interactive. items.title: Probing proximity-induced superconductivity in bilayer graphene using gate-defined quantum dots
items.abstract: Van der Waals heterostructures enable the combination of two-dimensional (2D) materials with different electronic properties in a single device. Bilayer graphene (BLG) is particularly attractive as its electrically tunable band gap enables local control of tunnel barriers and quantum dots (QDs). Here, we realize an all-2D hybrid platform based on BLG proximitized by superconducting NbSe$_2$. Using electrostatic gates, we define tunnel barriers and QDs at different distances from the superconductor-semiconductor interface. The QDs serve as local spectroscopic probes of the proximitized BLG channel, forming tunable superconductor-quantum dot-normal conductor junctions. Coulomb blockade and finite-bias spectroscopy reveal a proximity-induced superconducting gap of up to $80\,\mathrm{μeV}$ and allow to track its evolution with distance from the NbSe$_2$ contact. items.abstract: A prototype 185.7 MHz superconducting radio-frequency (SRF) electron gun cryomodule has been developed for the proposed LCLS-II-HE Low Emittance Injector at SLAC. It has an in-situ ultra-high-vacuum exchangeable cathode plug system compatible with semiconductor photocathodes. With a copper plug, the gun achieved continuous-wave RF operation at a cathode field of 30 MV/m. No measurable degradation was observed after plug removal and reinsertion with the cavity at 4.4 K. This result is a significant improvement over past continuous-wave SRF gun systems with exchangeable plugs.

items.abstract: Carrier mobility and optical absorption are key performance parameters of oxide semiconductors in transparent and flexible displays. We use a newly developed density-functional perturbation theory with a self-consistent Hubbard correction (DFPT+U) to study phonon-limited electron transport and phonon-assisted optical absorption in strained zinc oxide (ZnO).
